title: Refactor fontawesome icon usage.
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

- FontAwesome icons can now be embedded as SVG when the FontAwesome icon pack is **registered** in the Mermaid configuration. Otherwise, the icon will still be rendered using FontAwesome CSS (`<i>` tag).  
- Updated styles to properly set **fill color and positioning** for registered SVG icons. No extra styles are needed for FontAwesome CSS-based icons, as they inherit styles from FontAwesome.  
- **Only the flowchart diagram supports registered FontAwesome icons.**  

See https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/issues/474

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

### When text contains a FontAwesome icon reference:

- Check if the FontAwesome **icon pack** is registered in the Mermaid configuration.  
- If the **icon is registered**, replace it with a **stringified SVG representation**.  
- If the **icon is not found**, fallback to rendering it with **FontAwesome CSS** (`<i>` tag with the appropriate class).  

### Update to styles.

- We had a style defined that adds fill to all `path` elements inside `node` class. Now we are overriding this style to have `fill: currentColor` also reverting stroke and stroke-width to default

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [X] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html)
- [X] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
- [ ] :notebook: have added documentation. Make sure [`MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION`](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html#update-documentation) is used for all new features.
- [X] :butterfly: If your PR makes a change that should be noted in one or more packages' changelogs, generate a changeset by running `pnpm changeset` and following the prompts. Changesets that add features should be `minor` and those that fix bugs should be `patch`. Please prefix changeset messages with `feat:`, `fix:`, or `chore:`.

## Incomplete HTML attribute sanitization

Cross-site scripting vulnerability as the output of [this final HTML sanitizer step](1) may contain single quotes when it reaches this attribute definition.
Cross-site scripting vulnerability as the output of [this final HTML sanitizer step](2) may contain single quotes when it reaches this attribute definition.

[Show more details](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/security/code-scanning/188)
comments.label_reasoning: This is an XSS (cross-site scripting) vulnerability due to incomplete HTML attribute sanitization — single quotes in output can escape attribute context. Best mapped to injection vulnerability category.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
This is still a bit confusing.

Using this syntax, only FontAwesome icons are supported, but this documentation makes it seem like any icon pack is supported.

And it's a bit confusing with https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/2fb7bc2806f3d91dc9840ae988dc06e1329ca9a9/docs/syntax/flowchart.md?plain=1#L1943-L1955 too.

I think we also need to add a `<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>` to tell users what version of Mermaid supports this.

Maybe we can instead have something like:

````markdown
It is possible to add icons from fontawesome.

The icons are accessed via the syntax fa:#icon class name#.

```mermaid-example
flowchart TD
    B["fa:fa-twitter for peace"]
    B-->C[fa:fa-ban forbidden]
    B-->D(fa:fa-spinner)
    B-->E(A fa:fa-camera-retro perhaps?)
```

There are two ways to display these FontAwesome icons:

### Register FontAwesome icon packs (v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>+)

<Add instructions here (maybe with list of supported prefixes) and make a note that it will fallback to FontAwesome CSS if these aren't setup>

### Register FontAwesome CSS

Mermaid supports Font Awesome if the CSS is included on the website.
Mermaid does not have any restriction on the version of Font Awesome that can be used.

Please refer the [Official Font Awesome Documentation](https://fontawesome.com/start) on how to include it in your website.

Adding this snippet in the `<head>` would add support for Font Awesome v6.5.1

```html
<link
  href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/6.5.1/css/all.min.css"
  rel="stylesheet"
/>
```
````
comments.label_reasoning: The documentation is misleading — it implies any icon pack is supported when only FontAwesome is, and lacks version information. This is a documentation clarity issue.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
These tests are flaky:

![Flowchart-Icon-2-icon-verify-if-icons-are-working-from-fontawesome-library-forest-theme diff](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34fc0da3-578f-4b24-811a-98022ebfd729)

I think we need to:

- Instead of using https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/2fb7bc2806f3d91dc9840ae988dc06e1329ca9a9/cypress/platform/e2e.html#L9-L12, we might want to use a local version of FontAwesome, like what the docs site uses: https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/3eaf8b717770a119cd0ea5303632b6430330f239/packages/mermaid/src/docs/package.json#L21
- We might need something like `await Promise.all(Array.from(document.fonts, (font) => font.load()))` to forcibly wait for all fonts to load before starting to render the diagram: https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/blob/7b19bf7f230b95fde1ba1a4bbda78bc96e696773/src/index.js#L255
comments.label_reasoning: Flaky tests due to relying on an external CDN for FontAwesome and not waiting for fonts to load — improper test setup and resource loading practices.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
**issue(not sure if blocking or not)**: I don't know about this.

I feel like this might make it harder to debug issues where the font fails to load.

Maybe just doing:

```suggestion
  await loadFontAwesomeCSS();
  await Promise.all(Array.from(document.fonts, (font) => font.load()));
```

That way we get a JavaScript error when it fails to load and Cypress fails?

I don't know. @sidharthv96 and @saurabhg772244, what are your thoughts?
comments.label_reasoning: Swallowing font load errors silently makes it harder to detect failures; the suggestion is to let errors propagate rather than catching and ignoring them.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests a code change to surface errors more clearly rather than silently swallowing them, with a concrete code suggestion.

**question(blocking since it might causes us to get sued/DMCA-ed otherwise)**: Sorry! I missed this in my last review.

Even if we don't need to place a license here, I think we probably still need a comment here saying that.

You can use the [`@license` JSDoc tag](https://jsdoc.app/tags-license) (and [`@copyright`](https://jsdoc.app/tags-copyright) if you need that too, e.g. like the MIT license that Mermaid uses).
